open_points.subject: A16 owner-session upload lifetime
open_points.text: A16 says “from the session's end until that sweep the upload is reachable by no request,” while M11 says “Everything in it ends with the session” and A13 says a sign-out “leaves nothing in the ended session.”
open_points.question: Does an upload remain allocated after a time-limit ends its owner session, or must ending the session remove it immediately?
options: The upload remains inaccessible until the minute sweep removes it
Every kind of session end removes the upload immediately
Time-limit expiry delays removal, while sign-out and restart remove it immediately
open_points.default_guess: Use the explicit new A16 exception: time-limit expiry leaves an inaccessible upload until the sweep; sign-out and restart remove it immediately.

open_points.subject: A16 accepted import clearing other sessions
open_points.text: A16 says an accepted import “drops every session's upload” while holding the import lock and only “their session's lock”; A13 says requests that change one owner session's state are applied one at a time under that session's lock.
open_points.question: How is clearing uploads in owner sessions other than the confirming session synchronized with concurrent changes to those sessions?
options: The import lock alone owns every upload, so other sessions' locks are unnecessary
The accepted import must also acquire every affected session lock in a declared order
The global clear is a stated exception to A13's per-session serialization
open_points.default_guess: Treat uploaded files as exclusively protected by the import lock and make the global clear an explicit exception to per-session locking.

open_points.subject: A16 expired-session sweep
open_points.text: The upload of a session ended by its limits “is dropped by a sweep that takes the import lock once a minute”; the text does not say that the sweep takes the ended session's lock or how an ended session remains discoverable until the sweep.
open_points.question: What session state does the sweep inspect, and what synchronization protects removal of an expired session's upload?
options: Ended session shells remain until swept, and the import lock alone protects their uploads
The sweep also takes each session lock after the import lock
Expiry moves the upload to a separate import-lock-protected cleanup collection
open_points.default_guess: Keep expired uploads in a separate import-lock-protected cleanup collection and remove them on the next sweep.

open_points.subject: A17 environment-variable contract
open_points.text: The configuration is “the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_” and holds listed items, but the exact variable name for each item is never declared.
open_points.question: What exact environment-variable names represent the store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential and four service tokens?
options: Declare one fixed REGISTRY_ name for each item
Derive names mechanically from the prose labels
Allow implementation-selected names
open_points.default_guess: Declare fixed uppercase names such as REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION and one REGISTRY_*_TOKEN name per service.

open_points.subject: A17 owner-only configuration
open_points.text: Rule 1 permits “for an owner-only start, none of the four” service tokens, while rules 2 and 5 require “every item of rule 1 present” and say “A missing ... item fails the start.”
open_points.question: Are the four service-token variables optional as a complete group, or is every listed variable always required?
options: All four tokens present, or all four absent; a partial set fails
All four tokens are always required
Each token is independently optional
open_points.default_guess: Allow exactly two modes: all four service tokens present or all four absent; reject a partial set.

open_points.subject: A17 well-formed configuration values
open_points.text: Registry checks “each well formed,” but no well-formedness rules are given for locations, credentials, tokens or the backup key beyond secret length.
open_points.question: What exact syntax or decoding failures make each configuration item malformed?
options: All secrets are arbitrary nonempty environment strings meeting the byte-length rule, and locations follow a declared path grammar
Secrets must use a declared encoding such as base64 or hexadecimal
Each implementation chooses its accepted syntax
open_points.default_guess: Accept secrets as literal environment-string bytes after a declared UTF-8 encoding, and require locations to be valid filesystem paths.

open_points.subject: A17 secret length
open_points.text: A secret is “at least 32 bytes long,” although environment-variable values are text and no encoding or decoding rule defines those bytes.
open_points.question: Which byte representation is used to measure secret length and compare secrets for equality?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the literal environment value
Decoded bytes from a required base64 representation
Unicode characters rather than bytes
open_points.default_guess: Use the UTF-8 bytes of the literal environment value.

open_points.subject: A17 store location paths
open_points.text: Locations are compared “by their absolute paths with every symbolic link resolved,” but the text neither requires configured paths to be absolute nor says what base resolves a relative path.
open_points.question: Are relative store or backup locations refused, or against which stable directory are they resolved?
options: Require absolute configured paths
Resolve relative paths against the process working directory
Resolve relative paths against a release-defined data directory
open_points.default_guess: Require both configured locations to be absolute.

open_points.subject: A17 store format and version
open_points.text: The store must “open for reading and writing and carry the store version of the running release,” and a new empty store is made, but no store engine, durable format or version representation is declared.
open_points.question: What constitutes a valid Registry store, and how is its release-compatible version identified?
options: A release-declared SQLite database with an internal schema-version record
Another explicitly declared transactional store and version marker
An implementation-selected backend and version convention
open_points.default_guess: Use a SQLite database with an internal schema-version value fixed by the release.

open_points.subject: A17 startup-check precedence
open_points.text: Unknown items are checked “in the order of their names,” but the comparison used to order environment-variable names is not stated.
open_points.question: When several unknown REGISTRY_ variables exist, which one is the first reported failure?
options: Unicode code-point order
Bytewise order of environment names
Platform or environment enumeration order

open_points.subject: A18 backup cryptography
open_points.text: Each backup is “encrypted with the backup key” and records “a digest of the key,” but no encryption construction, nonce rule, authentication rule, key interpretation or digest algorithm is declared.
open_points.question: What exact authenticated-encryption and key-digest scheme defines a backup and detects a wrong key or altered ciphertext?
options: A release-declared authenticated-encryption container with a random nonce and a cryptographic key identifier
Encryption without authenticated integrity, relying on the restored store checks
An implementation-selected encryption library and format
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption container with a fresh random nonce and a cryptographic digest of the exact key bytes.

open_points.subject: A18 unencrypted backup record
open_points.text: A backup's instant, release, last sequence and key digest are “readable without its key,” but the text does not say whether those values are cryptographically bound to the encrypted store.
open_points.question: Must alteration or substitution of the unencrypted record make the backup check or restore fail?
options: Authenticate the record as associated data of the encrypted payload
Store the record unauthenticated and trust the backup directory
Duplicate the record inside the ciphertext and compare it after decryption
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate the entire unencrypted record as associated data and also verify its values against the decrypted store.

open_points.subject: A18 empty audit history
open_points.text: A backup records “the last audit sequence number it holds” and checks that “its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number,” but a new store can have no audit entry and therefore no last sequence number.
open_points.question: What is recorded and checked for a store whose audit log is empty?
options: Record sequence 0
Record an explicit absent value
Refuse to make a backup until an audit entry exists
open_points.default_guess: Record 0 and require both the audit counter and the absence of entries to agree with it.

open_points.subject: A18 store integrity check
open_points.text: The decrypted store must pass “the store's own integrity check,” but the accepted texts do not define that check or its required coverage.
open_points.question: Which exact conditions constitute the integrity check whose failure prevents keeping a backup?
options: The transactional store engine's full integrity check plus Registry schema and invariant validation
Only the storage engine's built-in integrity command
A release-selected check with no fixed minimum coverage
open_points.default_guess: Run the engine's full integrity check and verify the Registry schema version, audit counter and required database invariants.

open_points.subject: A18 validity of old kept backups
open_points.text: Rule 5 treats a kept record as valid when its four metadata values “can all be read,” while the formal invariant says “every kept backup is encrypted, consistent, checked”; older kept backups are never decrypted or integrity-checked again.
open_points.question: Is consistency guaranteed only when a backup is made, or must later runs detect corruption of an already-kept encrypted payload?
options: The guarantee is creation-time only; later payload corruption may remain until restore
Every run revalidates every kept backup
A persistent authenticated marker proves it passed creation-time checking but does not detect later corruption
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the guarantee as creation-time only and retain an authenticated marker that the creation check completed.

open_points.subject: A18 retention cutoff instant
open_points.text: The third step deletes backups “made more than 30 × 24 hours before,” without naming the reference instant used for that comparison.
open_points.question: At what instant is a backup's age evaluated during a run?
options: The instant the run began
The current clock instant when the deletion step examines each file
The new backup's recorded instant
open_points.default_guess: Use one UTC instant captured at the beginning of the run for every retention comparison in that run.

open_points.subject: A18 backup-file processing order
open_points.text: The run takes files “in the order of their names,” but no filename comparison is declared.
open_points.question: What total ordering is used when cleanup or retention processes several backup files?
options: Unicode code-point order
Bytewise filesystem-name order
The host filesystem's enumeration order
open_points.default_guess: Use ascending Unicode code-point order of the filename text.
